newsitem.title: UK: Britain says to extend water competition.
newsitem.headline: Britain says to extend water competition.

text.p: The British government said on Tuesday it intends to go ahead with proposals for extending competition in water and sewerage services in England and Wales.
Environment Secretary John Gummer said the government would bring forward legislation to proceed with the proposals in the next session of parliament.

The measures proposed include the introduction of common carriage arrangements to allow companies to use an existing supplier's pipe network to provide individual customers with a choice of water supply.
Similar provisions for sewerage services are also to be introduced.
The government also said it intended to extend the scope of arrangements under which a new water or waste undertaker can be appointed in an area served by an existing supplier.
Cross-border supply restrictions and the existing water supplier's monopoly on making connections to the water main are also to be removed.

"In developing this legislation we shall seek to provide a basis for competition both in waste water and clean water services, and to ensure that water quality continues to be safeguarded and that the charging regime continues to be fair and non-discriminatory," said Gummer.

He also said the governemnt intended to go further than its original proposals by following up suggestions made during consultation for extending the scope of common carriage and inset appointments to smaller users.
